An audio codec is a software or hardware tool that compresses and decompresses audio data. It converts analog sound waves into digital data (encoding) for storage or transmission, and then reconstructs the original sound (decoding) when played back. Audio codecs reduce file size while maintaining acceptable sound quality. Common examples include MP3, AAC, and WAV. They are essential for streaming, recording, and storing audio efficiently.

An audio codec is a tool that compresses and decompresses audio data. It converts analog sound waves into digital format (encoding) for efficient storage or transmission, and then reconstructs the original sound (decoding) when played back. This allows for smaller file sizes without significant loss in quality. Common codecs include MP3, AAC, and FLAC. MP3 is widely used for streaming and portable devices due to its balance of quality and file size. AAC offers better quality at similar sizes, and FLAC is lossless, preserving all original audio details. Codecs are essential in applications like music streaming, voice calls, and video content, where bandwidth and storage are limited.
